cause.label: dilution_or_going_concern
cause.what_happened: This is the third straight session of a post-consolidation collapse: the 25-for-1 Class A reverse split took effect on 2026-09-17, and the stock is down about 80% from the post-split level, with about 85% of the 1.02m-share Class A float trading today. No press release came out today. The only new document is a Schedule 13D/A filed on 2026-09-30. It restates that the CEO bought 1,625,000 Class B shares at $0.40 on 2026-09-25, not adjusted for the split, taking her to 58.7% as-converted and 99.3% of the votes.

evidence.claim: The 25-for-1 Class A consolidation took effect 2026-09-17; issued Class A shares went from 25,437,740 to 1,017,510

The 13D/A says Beverly Holding (owned by CEO Muchun Zhu) bought 1,625,000 Class B at $0.40 on 2026-09-25, for $650k. That gives 58.7% of Class A as-converted and 99.3% of the votes. The stated purpose is to restore majority control lost after the July offering and the Sept 17 consolidation
The subscription agreement is dated 2026-09-07 (before the split) at $0.40 a share, approved by the audit committee
Form 4: a Class B purchase of 1,625,000 at $0.40 on 2026-09-25, holding 1,831,598.04 afterwards

findings.finding: The Schedule 13D/A filed 2026-09-30 is the first document to put in one place that 1,625,000 new Class B shares were issued at $0.40, after a 25-for-1 consolidation that applied to Class A only. On an as-converted basis that is 1.6 times the entire 1.02m Class A float. Class A's economic share falls from about 83% to about 41%, and the CEO now holds 58.7% as-converted.
findings.mechanism_in_window: A wider audience reads the document. The 13D/A was filed on the drop day (2026-09-30), and aggregators republish 13D ownership percentages overnight. The Form 4 of 2026-09-25 gave only a Class B share count and gave no as-converted percentage.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Form 4 disclosing the same purchase was filed 2026-09-25. The next three sessions in the baseline were 09-28 -43.57%, 09-29 -24.40% and 09-30 -20.63%, so most of this is likely already in the price. That is why it is sized at -1 against a median absolute next-day move of 9.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The intraday tape has been momentum traders, and no wire story names the as-converted dilution. The Timothy Sykes/StocksToTrade coverage explicitly cites no catalyst. If the price fully held a Class A claim on about 41% of the economic equity rather than 83%, the post-split fall would already have stopped and the stock would trade calmly on falling volume. Instead the float is turning over almost once a day.
findings.independence: The Form 4 of 2026-09-25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2018529/000149315226044229/xslF345X06/ownership.xml) and the 6-K of 2026-09-11 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2018529/000121390026099320/ea0305176-6k_intercont.htm) show the same transaction. They are the same issuer and the same event, so this is not independent confirmation of the price effect.

outside_window.finding: The S-8 of 2026-09-11 registers 5,087,548 Class A shares under the 2026 Stock Incentive Plan. That is about 203k after the split if the plan adjusts, or about 20% of the float. No lock-up or reoffer prospectus is mentioned. Grants can be issued and sold at any time, but there is no dated issuance.

The effective $200m F-3 shelf (EFFECT 2026-09-10) has no 424B prospectus supplement or ATM sales agreement filed. Any takedown needs a supplement first, and the baby-shelf limit (one-third of a public float of roughly $1.5m) caps it at a trivial size.

The July 2026 unit warrants (8m before either split, zero exercise price option, two shares per warrant) expire six months after issuance, about 2027-01-08. The remaining unexercised count is not disclosed.
The 180-day lock-up on officers, directors and certain holders from the July 8 offering close ends about 2027-01-04. After that the CEO's Class B, convertible 1:1, can reach the Class A market.

This is the second 25:1 consolidation in 2026 (April 2 and September 17), a cumulative 625:1. If the bid falls back under $1, Nasdaq's rules for companies that have reverse-split recently point to no compliance period. That needs a sustained breach and is not dated. The stock is at $1.50, and no deficiency or panel notice was found in the issuer's filings.

baseline_tension: The finding agrees with the reaction function: high ATR, a negative median across the name's own falls, and heavy float turnover all point the same way. But the name's own history includes violent bounces (+18.5%, +19.9%, +16.5%), and the dilution was disclosed on 09-25, so the research read is kept small (-1.0).
